feedback:
Written before this candidate races, so no result is stated for it. The candidate is iteration 8 (kd 1.2, score 495.2, the best raced design) with one change: kd 1.2 to 1.4. The evidence for raising kd is a clean trend on the same geometry and gains. S-bend progress went 0.46 (kd 0.8, iter 3), 0.61 (kd 1.0 with y 0.06, iter 7), and 0.84 (kd 1.2, iter 8), and the oval stayed at 20/20 with steering_oscillation falling slightly (0.197 to 0.189, iter 7 to 8). Iteration 4 cut the oval to 13/20 when kp went to 5.5 and base_speed to 1.05 together with kd 1.0, so that damage is not evidence against kd alone. Iteration 6 showed that widening the sensor span hurts the oval, so the geometry stays fixed. The candidate is valid, every value is inside the contract, and it changes one field. Approve it. The race is the next source of information, and the single-field trend has been monotonic so far.

After the race, read the results in this order. (a) If the oval holds at 20/20 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3 and s-bend progress rises above 0.9 with line_loss_events below 1, the kd trend still holds. Consider a small further step such as kd 1.6 in the final revision, not a kp change. (b) If oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 or oval completion drops below 1.0, higher kd is amplifying sensor noise. Revert to kd 1.2, which is the best raced design, and do not raise kp. (c) If s-bend progress is flat within about 0.05 of 0.84 while the oval holds, derivative damping is no longer the limit. Test a narrower wheel_track of 0.09 with mass held at 0.6, because iteration 5 showed that wheel_track 0.09 combined with mass 0.5 cost oval reliability. Slalom remains the hardest track at progress about 0.15. If it stays there, the next lever is a lower base_speed or a different line_loss mode, tested one field at a time.
requested_changes: If the oval holds at 20/20 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3 and s-bend progress rises above 0.9 with line_loss_events below 1: keep kd 1.4 and try kd 1.6 next, since kd alone improved s-bend progress from 0.61 (kd 1.0) to 0.84 (kd 1.2) without losing the oval.

If oval steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.3 or oval completion drops below 1.0: revert kd to 1.2, the best raced design, and keep y 0.06, because higher derivative gain may amplify sensor noise. Do not raise kp, since iteration 4 showed kp 5.5 with speed 1.05 cut the oval to 13/20.

If s-bend progress stays within about 0.05 of 0.84 with the oval holding: return kd to 1.2 and test wheel_track 0.09 with mass held at 0.6, because iterations 1 to 3 showed a narrower track raised bend progress without losing the oval.
